title: RRSI: 噪声带内的逐轮决策（port）
note: HarnessGrad mode-A port 移植逐轮规则，并通过单 step report_many 的 incumbent_round 记录最新历史候选重裁决后的保留轮次；没有可用判定则不声明保留并记录原因。平台已有批量提交与历史树能力，但此入口仍一次只草拟一个候选，不恢复选中树，也未接通上游同 incumbent 的 m-candidate 评估后选优。独立的 methods/rrsi/fidelity.py 提供离线候选池选择等纯函数；这仍不是 native reproduction。

source.scope: native algorithm source audit; local checkout may contain unrelated uncommitted probes

preserved: noise floor, two-branch cost rule, structural novelty, and study-side score discipline
m-candidate argmax over admissible candidates and incumbent retention when none qualify (offline pure module)
adapted: annealed budget, stall/exploration reserve, pruning state, and bounded critic repair are wired in the one-candidate-per-call mode-A port only
pre-evaluation deterministic plus model critic is retained in the port, while native multi-candidate retry/deploy wiring is missing
HarnessGrad artifact/channel and configurable model, scaffold, domain evaluator and split
platform trial-spread calibration is an explicit provenance-labeled adapter
role prompts are compact adaptations of the upstream action contracts, not verbatim templates
missing token accounting is explicitly marked unavailable instead of using the upstream dC=0 substitution
incumbent_round records delayed singleton re-adjudication against the actual predecessor; it does not restore a historical tree or select the newly submitted unmeasured candidate
missing_until_runtime_support: runtime wiring to draft/group m screened artifacts from one incumbent, evaluate on the study side, and select after measurements become visible (batch submission already exists)
restoration/deployment of the retained incumbent via available states/ trees; kept_round records a choice but does not deploy it
native analyst/digester trace dispatch, git worktrees/frontier, and k trials inside the RRSI loop
full upstream role prompt bodies and domain-specific role briefs

deviations.what: The run.py port still drafts one candidate per call and records delayed singleton retention instead of executing the native measured m-candidate selection and deployment loop.
deviations.why: The platform supports report_many batches (methods/editor.py:1485-1530), records incumbent_round as kept_round without deploying it (harnessgrad/loops/mode_a.py:524-544), and exposes historical trees through states/ (harnessgrad/channel.py:427-450). A batch exposes no intervening measurement to the method. Upstream rrsi/loop.py:290-307 drafts/screens m variants from one incumbent, evaluates them, then calls rrsi/selection.py:124-137 for an admissible argmax; rrsi/loop.py:327-340 deploys the winner or retains H_t. This port neither groups such a pool for later selection nor restores a selected states/ tree. It only re-adjudicates the latest measured historical candidate against its predecessor and emits that retention as incumbent_round. The offline fidelity.py selector is not wired into main().

deviations.what: Missing token accounting leaves admissibility and retention undeclared after the score floor passes.
deviations.why: Upstream rrsi/evaluate.py:131-135 substitutes dC=0 when either token count is unavailable. run.py:_relative_cost_change and _judge instead mark cost_rule_active=false and admissible=null; _retention then omits incumbent_round with the cost_skipped reason. This avoids claiming a cost verdict without its inputs but cannot reproduce upstream selection in that case.

deviations.what: The noise band uses an explicit override or a platform trial-spread adapter, with a declared fallback, rather than staging upstream base calibration.
deviations.why: run.py:_delta uses HG_RRSI_DELTA when set; otherwise z*sqrt(2)*score_std of the latest point when score_std>0 and n_trials>1, or HG_RRSI_DELTA_FALLBACK (default 0). Upstream rrsi/calibrate.py:85-108 estimates from repeated base scores or per-task trial bootstrap. The adapter and fallback do not establish equivalence to that base-calibration procedure.

deviations.what: Native scaffold and evaluator are not silently replaced.
deviations.why: The port keeps model, scaffold, domain evaluator and split configurable; a result is a decision-rule alignment measurement until those axes match the source instance.
